verdict.summary: You can create a Notion public connection and use it with other users' workspaces without listing it. Notion's docs don't mention a review step for this. A security review applies only if you want a Marketplace listing. The one setting you can't undo is installation scope: choose "Any workspace" at creation if you may ever list the connection.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for an unlisted connection; plus a few hours to prepare Marketplace listing assets if you list
verdict.approval_wait: None for unlisted use. 5-10 business days (stated by Notion) for a Marketplace listing review

gates.name: Public connection created (development workspace)
gates.unlocks: You can authorize your own Notion workspace through Composio using your own client ID and secret.
limits: Installation scope (Any workspace vs. Selected workspaces only) is fixed at creation and can't be changed later
The connection can only reach pages the user picks in the page picker during authorization

gates.name: Unlisted public connection shared with invited users
gates.unlocks: Other users can authorize through your connection. Each gets their own access token for their own workspace.
limits: The fetched docs don't mention a test-user allowlist, install cap or warning screen
The token endpoint can return a 403 with code test_env_error. The docs don't explain it, and it may point to a test-environment restriction
A "Selected workspaces only" connection can't be listed on the Marketplace later
gates.time_to_reach: Same day as Gate 1. No extra step is documented

gates.name: Any-workspace public connection (optionally listed on the Notion Marketplace)
gates.unlocks: Any Notion user can install the connection. Listing it on the Marketplace also makes it discoverable inside Notion.
limits: A Marketplace listing requires installation scope "Any workspace" and a Notion security review
The Authorization URL field on the Configuration tab fills in only after you submit for review. You can build the authorize URL yourself before then
Listings can be rejected for brand or trademark issues, quality concerns or failing baseline connection criteria
gates.time_to_reach: Immediately for unlisted public use. About 5-10 business days after submission for a Marketplace listing

steps.title: Open the Developer portal and start a new public connection
steps.detail: Sign in to Notion and open the Developer portal. In the Build section of the sidebar, select Public connections, then click Create new connection. Enter a connection name and choose your development workspace.
gotchas: Don't use an internal connection or a personal access token for a multi-user agent. Those are static credentials limited to one workspace or one user.

steps.title: Choose the installation scope (can't be changed later)
steps.detail: Pick "Any workspace" if anyone outside your chosen workspaces might use the agent, or if you may ever want a Marketplace listing. Pick "Selected workspaces only" only for strictly private use.
gotchas: Installation scope is set once at creation. Fixing a wrong choice means creating a new connection and having users re-authorize.

steps.title: Set the redirect URI
steps.detail: In the creation form's redirect URI field, paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config. It must match exactly the redirect_uri sent in the token request.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: A community guide says redirect URIs need a protocol and can't contain fragments, relative paths, wildcards or a public IP address.

steps.title: Choose the fewest capabilities you need
steps.detail: Notion controls access with capabilities (read, update and insert content, comments, and user info level), not OAuth scope strings. Turn on only what the agent's tools use. Notion says fewer capabilities make workspace admins more likely to install.
gotchas: If you change capabilities later, every existing user has to re-authenticate.

steps.title: Prepare company and legal details
steps.detail: Draft a tagline, privacy policy URL, terms of use URL, support email, company name and website. A community tutorial says the form requires these, and that the website link appears on the authentication screens.
gotchas: These fields come from a community tutorial written for the older "integrations" UI. The current form may differ.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and secret into Composio
steps.detail: After creating the connection, open its Configuration tab. Copy the OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret into a Composio auth config for the notion toolkit. Leave scopes empty. Notion's token endpoint uses HTTP Basic auth with these credentials.
gotchas: The Authorization URL field on the Configuration tab stays empty until you submit for review. Composio builds the authorize URL from https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize instead.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection from Composio. Click Allow access, then finish the page picker by selecting the pages or databases the agent should reach. Check that the token response returns an access_token, workspace_id and bot_id, then make one API call.
gotchas: If the user clicks Allow access but doesn't finish page selection, the connection gets no page access.
The page picker shows only pages the user has full access to.

steps.title: Share the connection with invited users
steps.detail: Send other users the Composio connect link. Each person who authorizes gets their own access token for their own workspace. Make sure your token storage keeps the rotated refresh token: each refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token.
gotchas: If the token endpoint returns 403 test_env_error, note the context. Notion's docs don't explain this code.

steps.title: (Optional) Offer a template page
steps.detail: If your agent expects a particular page structure, set a public Notion page as the template. Users can then duplicate it during authorization instead of picking pages.

steps.title: (Optional, listing only) Create a Marketplace listing draft
steps.detail: Only needed if you want the connection discoverable on the Notion Marketplace. Create a listing with a name, description, category, tags, listing images and logo, and link it to your Any-workspace public connection. The listing is saved as a draft until you submit it.

steps.title: (Optional, listing only) Submit for review
steps.detail: Submit the listing draft. This triggers Notion's security review of the public connection. Submitting is also when the Authorization URL field fills in on the Configuration tab.

steps.title: Wait for Notion's review
steps.detail: Notion says to expect an email reply within 5-10 business days. If changes are needed, the team sends feedback and you can resubmit after making updates.

requirements.item: Notion account with a development workspace
requirements.detail: You select the development workspace when you create the public connection.
It must exactly match the redirect_uri used in the token request.
Choose Any workspace or Selected workspaces only. You can't change it after creation.

requirements.item: Tagline, privacy policy URL, terms of use URL, support email, company name and website
requirements.detail: Required according to a community tutorial. Not confirmed in Notion's official docs.
Each refresh returns a new refresh token, which you must store in place of the old one.
Name, description, category and tags, listing images and logo, and an associated public connection.
Required before a Marketplace listing, not for unlisted use.

scopes.effect: Lets the agent read pages and databases the user selected. The docs don't say whether any capability triggers extra review.
Needed for agents that edit or create pages. Request these only if your tools write to Notion. Changing them later forces users to re-authenticate.
Needed to read or create comments. Request only if used.

scopes.scope: User capabilities (no user info / without email / with email)
scopes.effect: Sets what user objects show and grants access to the List all users and Retrieve a user endpoints. The docs don't say whether the with-email level affects review.

blockers.symptom: You can't list the connection on the Marketplace
blockers.cause: The connection was created with installation scope "Selected workspaces only", and this can't be changed.
blockers.fix: Create a new public connection with "Any workspace" scope, update the Composio auth config, and have users re-authorize.

blockers.symptom: The agent gets object-not-found or empty results after a successful connect
blockers.cause: The user clicked Allow access but didn't finish the page picker, or picked no relevant pages.
blockers.fix: Have the user reconnect and select the needed pages or databases, or offer a template page.

blockers.symptom: Existing users lose access or are prompted again after a config change
blockers.cause: The public connection's capabilities were changed after users authorized it.
blockers.fix: Settle on capabilities before rollout, and plan a re-authentication prompt whenever you change them.

blockers.symptom: Token endpoint returns 401 invalid_client or 403 test_env_error
blockers.cause: invalid_client: wrong client ID or secret in HTTP Basic auth. test_env_error: Notion's docs don't explain this code.
blockers.fix: Re-copy the credentials from the Configuration tab. For test_env_error, note the context and contact Notion developer support.

blockers.cause: Brand or trademark issues, quality concerns, or failing baseline connection criteria.
Community sources report a rate limit averaging 3 requests per second per integration, which they say can't be raised by paying.
blockers.fix: Add backoff and request queuing. Confirm the limit on Notion's official request-limits page.

composio.note: Composio's managed Notion OAuth app is fine for prototyping. Notion's consent screen will show Composio's connection rather than your brand. Register your own public connection when you want your own name and logo on the consent screen, your own client ID and secret and token ownership, control over capabilities, or a Marketplace listing (which requires Any-workspace scope and a security review). The scope list stays empty either way, because Notion access comes from capabilities and page selection.
